items.name: openset-llm
items.description: Fast local LLM inference on plain CPUs. No GPU, 8 GB of RAM. OpenAI-compatible server.

readme.excerpt:
git clone https://github.com/opensetlabs/openset-llm && cd openset-llm && ./start

An LLM is not a sealed box. It is a stack of parts you can rewrite: matmul kernels, decoding, attention, caches. People already rewire single neurons to change what a model does; we rewired the machinery underneath to change where it runs. Do that, and a 27B model runs on the hardware the world already owns, ordinary CPUs, not just GPUs. Search, extraction, agents and speech then run locally with no per-token fee, and products that never paid off at API prices do.

It fits where a 27B model usually does not. Everything here runs in 8 GB of system memory with no GPU at all: no video memory, no unified memory, nothing offloaded. A standard 4-bit build of the same Qwen3.8-27B is a 16–19 GB file, which is why models of this size are normally run on a GPU or a 24–32 GB machine. (Another 26B model can be squeezed into 8 GB at 1 bit per weight; we measured it on the same box: Numbers.) Mainline llama.cpp's own packing of this ternary model is 7.63 GB and pages from disk on the same 8 GB machine (measured); the file this engine runs is 5.95 GB.
features: ik's greedy outputs differ from ours (different arithmetic after its repack), but its WikiText-2 perplexity is 7.5681 vs
--multi 4 : each stream's greedy output is byte-identical to the same request alone.
We are making this path faster.
Measurements on real AVX2-only desktop and laptop chips come next, and we will publish the numbers here.
Phones are the next target we are working on.
Context: 4,096 tokens by default on purpose: a full 4k context with speculation leaves ~0.2 GB free on an 8 GB
Longer context on 8 GB (experimental, opt-in): a smaller attention cache leaves room for more context and

items.name: solid-glass
items.description: A design system for AI applications. Material, physical, tactile, technical.

readme.excerpt:
A refined glass-inspired aesthetic that feels solid from afar and reveals its subtle materiality up close. Delicate highlights, fine borders, and soft shadows create depth, while a restrained finish emphasizes clarity, stability, and a sense of solidity over transparency, refraction, and fluidity.

That is one of the blocks: whole screens made of the components, to look at, read and copy in. Below, the components themselves.

It stands between flat design and liquid glass. Flat is an opaque block with no finish to speak of; liquid glass is nearly clear, and on a page with a lot of text the reader is always fighting the background for the words. Solid Glass lets only an outline through: enough to know it is glass, not enough to get in the way of reading.

Your job search, on your own server: one profile, a tailored resume and cover letter for every job, and every application tracked from draft to offer.

Dossier keeps your career history in one profile and turns it into a clean resume. items.name: dms
items.description: Open-source back office for your product. Connect Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB or MongoDB, mock up the dashboard with your coding agent, then it builds the pages as TypeScript in your repo. Self-hosted.

readme.excerpt:
The open-source back office for your product. Paste your PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB or RethinkDB connection string. Your coding agent drafts a live mockup you comment on, then builds the admin pages and dashboards as TypeScript in your repo.

npx @antelopejs/core project init demo --template dms-connect-demo

Then cd demo && docker compose up starts AntelopeJS DMS and a sample coffee shop in PostgreSQL.
features: A change redraws at once, with no typecheck and no reload.
Blocks read sample data, so you settle the dashboard before wiring a table or a query.
Pin a comment on any block and press Resolve with AI . Once you approve the mockup, Build it writes the real code once.
In the assistant's popup, choose Start from an existing database , paste the connection string and press Connect and analyse .
Choose Generate a first mockup . The assistant runs Claude Code or Codex on your own account, and the mockup fills up while it writes it.
Press Build it . We approved the mockup as written, and took the assistant's suggested answer to each of its three questions about the plan.
Existing product? Connect its database. You get a page for every table you keep, plus dashboards.
New product? Start from the template and build the tables and pages from nothing.

Runs your own Switch copy natively on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Android and HarmonyOS — full touch controls, 60 fps, new endgame modes. Bring your own game files. 开源的《暗黑破坏神 II：狱火重生》术士君临 iOS / macOS / 安卓 / 鸿蒙兼容层

readme.excerpt:
An open-source compatibility layer for Diablo II: Resurrected with the Reign of the Warlock expansion, for iOS, macOS, Android and HarmonyOS. It brings the Nintendo Switch release you bought, expansion included, to iPhone, iPad and Mac in full: the original game code runs natively, every control is rebuilt for touch, the frame rate holds at 60 fps, and you are in a game one second after the main menu. There is now a native macOS version as well (first version): on an Apple silicon Mac it starts on double-click and works with keyboard, mouse and gamepad. Since v2.0 there is an Android version (community port): the same game program executes natively on ARM64 Android phones, with the graphics reimplemented on Vulkan; on a Snapdragon 8+ Gen 1 phone the camp and the Den of Evil and Cow Level fights all run at a median 60 fps (see "Android" below); a HarmonyOS version runs on the same engine (community port: an unsigned shell from the Releases page that you re-sign yourself, nothing to build; see "HarmonyOS"). Apple TV 4K (3rd generation, A15) has a community port (developer preview) that has reached the character-selection screen only on its author's device; see the device table below.

This is not a tech demo that "sort of runs". It is a mobile version polished for daily play, from your first character all the way through the endgame.

items.name: SideInstaller
items.description: An an app that installs Sidestore on iOS 27, fully on-device

readme.excerpt:
Install SideStore and LiveContainer directly on your iPhone. No PC required.

SideStore and LiveContainer are currently the best way to sideload on iOS. However, there's one big problem: installing them requires a PC, which many people don't have. That's why I made SideInstaller, a free and open-source iOS app that installs them directly on your iPhone, no PC required.

SideInstaller handles the entire setup process on-device. It takes care of the pairing, provisioning, and installation steps that normally force you to plug into a computer and run desktop tools, all from a single app running on the phone itself. Once it's done, you get a fully working SideStore and LiveContainer setup ready to sideload your own apps.
